meta.title: Mobile Access
meta.description: Pair an iPhone or iPad on the same LAN so Safari can securely open the official DeepSeek Harness Web GUI.

ui.title: Mobile Access
ui.subtitle: Open this Mac’s official DSH from an iPhone or iPad on the same LAN.
ui.urlHint: Type this address into Safari on the iPhone.
ui.codeHint: Enter these 8 digits on the iPhone pairing page.
ui.copyFailed: Copy failed; select the text manually
ui.step1: Put the iPhone and the Mac on the same Wi-Fi, without client isolation.
ui.step2: Open the address in Safari, enter the code, and tap “Connect DSH”.
ui.step3: After pairing, use Safari Share → “Add to Home Screen”.
ui.loopbackBody: DSH is listening on loopback only. The plugin is starting a LAN gateway; if it fails, diagnostics appear here. The Mac keeps using 127.0.0.1.
ui.gatewayBody: DSH still listens only on 127.0.0.1. The iPhone uses the LAN address below; the Mac keeps its original address.
ui.httpBody: This is plain-HTTP LAN access. DSH already handles UUIDs and most copy buttons; this plugin adds a fallback for older direct navigator.clipboard calls on iPhone.
ui.selftestNote: The self-test only reads browser capabilities; it does not change DSH or affect the Mac.
ui.limit1: iOS Safari has no desktop drag-and-drop; use the system file picker.
ui.limit2: iOS suspends background pages; keep DSH in the foreground for long tasks.
ui.limit3: Safari hands downloads to the Files app; iOS chooses the location.
ui.zeroImpactBody: The plugin adds exactly three routes, one sidebar entry, and one main panel. It does not modify core code, auth, config, theme, layout, or other plugins, and it never polls in the background.
